W Residences Marina View - Singapore unveils branded residential luxury at its sales gallery
article:
On entering the sales gallery for W Residences Marina View - Singapore , visitors encounter a space that departs from the conventional showflat format.

A tunnel-like passage opens into a grand, expansive event space, where a large-scale architectural model of the development takes centre stage.

Opposite the model, a circular bar offers a touch of hospitality during viewings, mirroring the social and lifestyle-oriented experience envisioned for future residents.

Get the latest details on available units and prices for W Residences Marina View - Singapore

The showflats draw inspiration from the cosmopolitan character of Marina Bay. Their designs capture the precinct’s urban setting, vibrant energy and contemporary lifestyle.

These features impressed the panel of judges at the EdgeProp Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026, securing W Residences Marina View - Singapore the Showflat Excellence title.

The accolade recognises projects that effectively convey their design vision to prospective buyers, with assessments based on space utilisation, creativity, originality and practicality.

Sandy Tan, EPEA 2026 judge and founder of interior design firm Chalked, described the project’s show units as “a standout”.

High-end homes with bespoke services

Developed by IOI Properties Group and operated by Marriott International, W Residences Marina View - Singapore is a 51-storey integrated tower that will comprise 683 branded residences set above a five-star W Hotel.

The branded development, which is under construction, will have one- to three-bedroom units ranging from 538 to 1,249 sq ft, as well as four- and five-bedroom units spanning 2,250 to 2,809 sq ft. It will also include three penthouses: a simplex 5,199 sq ft unit and two duplex units measuring 5,350 sq ft each.

Designed to blend five-star hotel services with the comforts of home, the ultra-luxury development pairs bold design with curated lifestyle experiences. Services include round-the-clock concierge assistance and a suite of more than 50 lifestyle and wellness facilities.

The project sits on an 84,148 sq ft site located along Marina View, just a three-minute drive from the sales gallery on Bayfront Avenue.

The public launch of W Residences Marina View - Singapore took place in October last year, with an initial release of 100 units.

This followed a private VVIP preview in July, during which two units were sold: a 1,195 sq ft three-bedder for $3.99 million and an 850 sq ft, premium two-bedroom unit for $2.85 million. Caveats lodged show that the project has sold 15 units as at Oct 26 at an average price of $3,082 psf.

Personalising luxury through design

The sales gallery and all four showflats’ interiors were designed by Hachem Studio. The showflats highlight the one- to three-bedroom and five-bedroom layouts, each tailored to reflect distinct lifestyles and preferences.

Fady Hachem, principal director and founder of Hachem Studio, says the design concept behind the interiors was shaped by the development’s location at Marina Bay, which attracts a “diverse community of successful professionals, entrepreneurs and international homeowners”.

He adds: “Rather than adopting a singular design language across all four residences, we explored different material palettes, colours and furnishings to complement the personalities of the imagined homeowners.”

The three-bedroom show unit, themed “The Motorsport Enthusiast Family”, demonstrates how a home can be tailored to express its occupants’ interests and passions.

At the heart of the design is a hobby room featuring F1-inspired memorabilia, decorative pieces and a car racing simulator, offering potential buyers an interactive way to experience the space.

“For us, luxury is not only about beautiful finishes and furnishings, but also about creating spaces that support individuality, hobbies and meaningful experiences,” Hachem explains.

Where craftsmanship meets creativity

Meanwhile, the five-bedroom show unit is distinguished by its use of spatial planning, refined materials and statement design elements.

Designed for a family that enjoys entertaining, it includes a dedicated cigar and whisky room.

The room incorporates a functional design feature: a large statement artwork that doubles as a sliding partition, which gives the flexibility to either open up or enclose the space.

In the master bedroom, textured glass separates it from the adjoining bathroom, letting light filter through while preserving privacy.

Timber finishes, curated furnishings and contemporary elements lend the showflat a “layer of sophistication”, while ensuring that each space feels “luxurious without being overly formal or predictable”, Hachem notes.

Chalked’s Tan praises the thoughtful use of metal and textured materials, as well as the quality of craftsmanship across the show units.

Another highlight is the distinctive design of the show units. “It is refreshing to see a developer push creativity this far,” she says.

title: Zyon Grand: Integrated development with luxury residences that tick all the boxes
article:
Residences at Zyon Grand , an integrated development along Kim Seng Road in District 3, were an instant hit when they launched. Buyers snapped up 84% of the 706 units available during the launch weekend in October 2025, with prices averaging $3,050 psf.

A year on, Zyon Grand is about 90% taken up. Caveats lodged as at Oct 23 show an average price of $3,066 psf for units sold.

The 99-year leasehold development was crowned the Top Selling Project for the Rest of Central Region (RCR) at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026. The award is based on developers’ sales of new projects over a 12-month period.

Zyon Grand also bagged two other wins at the EPEA 2026: the Sustainability Excellence award for residential mixed-use developments and the People’s Choice award for uncompleted residential projects.

Developed by City Developments Ltd (CDL) and Mitsui Fudosan Group, Zyon Grand features twin 62-storey residential towers, a 36-storey long-stay serviced apartment block and ground-floor retail space.

Attractive location, strong connectivity

Zyon Grand’s major draw is its location, says Sky Seah, academic director at the National University of Singapore and part of the EPEA judging panel.

Though classified as an RCR site, Zyon Grand sits right at the edge of the Core Central Region. The development is a short commute from the CBD and the Orchard Road shopping belt. It also has easy access to lifestyle offerings in nearby neighbourhoods such as Great World, River Valley and Robertson Quay.

The development’s connectivity is another major advantage. Zyon Grand is integrated with Havelock MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line, which is just two stops from Orchard MRT Station, an interchange with the North-South Line. The project is also one stop from Outram Park MRT Station, which is an interchange for the East-West and North-East lines.

Meanwhile, the retail podium, called Zyon Galleria, will offer restaurants, a supermarket and an early-childhood development centre.

Piloting long-stay serviced apartments

Zyon Grand occupies a 164,450 sq ft site that CDL and Mitsui Fudosan purchased through a Government Land Sale (GLS) tender in April 2024.

The partners paid about $1.11 billion, or $1,202 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr), for the 99-year leasehold plot known as Zion Road (Parcel A).

Not long after, Zion Road (Parcel B), a neighbouring plot under the Reserve List of the 1H2024 GLS Programme, was triggered for sale. It was eventually awarded to Allgreen Properties in July 2024 for 730.1million(1,304 psf ppr).

The plot is now the site of the 596-unit Promenade Peak , which launched for sale in August 2025.

Zyon Grand’s site was the first GLS parcel to be sold with a long-stay serviced apartment component, as part of URA’s pilot for its Serviced Apartments II (SA2) housing typology.

SA2 units cater to guests staying for at least three months, compared with the seven-day minimum for standard serviced apartments. Unlike standard serviced apartments, SA2 units do not need to be fully self-contained apartments with kitchen amenities.

‘Neat’ separation

Zyon Grand was designed by Japan’s Nikken Sekkei in collaboration with Singapore’s ADDP Architects.

The pair also partnered on Newport Plaza, CDL’s mixed-use project on the former Fuji Xerox Towers site in the CBD. The 215m, 45-storey development comprises the 246-unit Newport Residences , along with offices, serviced apartments and restaurants.

Newport Residences was also a winner at the EPEA 2026, with judges praising its innovative design that seamlessly incorporates various uses in a single building.

In contrast, Nikken Sekkei and ADDP Architects took a different approach with Zyon Grand.

Here, the firms focused on “making full use of the site’s expansiveness to neatly separate the residences from the serviced apartments”, observes Mark Ong, EPEA 2026 judge and group director at architectural and engineering firm P&T Consultants.

The SA2 block is located at the eastern end of the site. While the entire development has a single main entrance along Kim Seng Road, the residential towers have a separate arrival area from Zyon Galleria and the SA2 block.

The SA2 block also has its own amenities, ensuring the condo facilities are exclusively for residents.

Expressing orchids and ikebana

On completion, Zyon Grand’s twin residential towers will be among the tallest structures in the River Valley-Zion Road area. Standing at 240m, the 62-storey skyscrapers will be a stately addition to the skyline.

They feature a distinctive façade with undulating fins, inspired by the Vanda Miss Joaquim orchid, Singapore’s national flower. Mimicking its petals, the fins add an organic visual element to the buildings.

The slender vertical shapes of all three towers draw from the principles of ikebana, the Japanese art of flower arrangement. Emphasising restraint, balance and harmony with nature, ikebana is often expressed through asymmetry and negative space.

Zyon Grand’s landscaping, helmed by Ecoplan Asia, also pays homage to the national flower, with orchid-shaped planters and water features woven into the design.

More broadly, the landscaping is designed to resemble a tropical rainforest, with multi-tiered green and blue spaces that evoke river valleys and lush terrain.

Premium homes and facilities

Residences at Zyon Grand range from one-bedroom-plus-study apartments of 474 sq ft to five-bedroom supreme apartments of 1,819 sq ft. A five-bedroom penthouse sits at the top of each tower — one measures 2,659 sq ft, while the other spans 2,756 sq ft.

The towers have a north-south orientation. High-floor units facing the southern coastline will have views that include Sentosa, the CBD and Marina Bay.

The project’s interior designer, 2nd Edition, also drew on ikebana principles. The homes have a minimalist design focused on seamless integration, such as large-format wall tiles and sinks that sit flush with countertops to minimise visible joints.

Each home comes with a Haiku ceiling fan; V-Zug and Liebherr appliances; and bathroom fittings from Hansgrohe and Geberit. The kitchens and bathrooms also feature an integrated magnetic accessories wall system with movable shelves.

Extensive lifestyle facilities complement the well-appointed homes. On the main facilities deck on the first floor, these include a clubhouse, multiple pools, a tennis and pickleball court, a yoga studio and a gym.

Sky terraces located on Levels 22 and 43 of both towers offer more facilities, including an outdoor fitness area, a meditation deck and panoramic lookout points.

End-to-end sustainability

Zyon Grand has been awarded the Building and Construction Authority’s Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy certification, along with badges for Health & Wellbeing, Whole Life Carbon and Maintainability.

The development’s sustainability credentials reflect end-to-end green features that span passive design, efficient systems, deliberate material choices and lower-carbon construction.

Over half of the development is built using prefabricated construction, increasing efficiency and reducing waste. Building materials include those endorsed by the Singapore Green Building Council.

To reduce reliance on air conditioning, design features were chosen to help naturally reduce solar heat gain and promote airflow. These include recessed balconies and ledges that provide shade, porous building and home layouts, and ample green and communal spaces.

Energy-efficient systems back these up. They include high-efficiency air conditioning systems, LED lighting and occupancy sensors in common areas.

River Valley transformation

Zyon Grand is part of a wave of new developments that are reshaping the River Valley-Zion Road precinct. In addition to the 596-unit Promenade Peak, two other developments launched in the area over the past year: the 455-unit River Modern in March 2026 and the 524-unit River Green in August 2025.

Like Zyon Grand, all three projects have been well received, with take-up rates currently ranging from around 73% (Promenade Peak) to 95% (River Modern and River Green), based on lodged caveats.

Another GLS site, River Valley (Parcel C), was awarded in June to a joint venture between Sunway MCL and CSC Land Group at $1,730 psf ppr. The partners are expected to launch a residential development with over 500 units across two 36-storey towers.

The new projects are extending the River Valley residential precinct towards Havelock, says EPEA judge Seah. She expects this to “create a dense and more vibrant neighbourhood” that would appeal to both homebuyers and tourists.

In any case, Zyon Grand’s well-rounded appeal has proven to resonate deeply with buyers. “As an integrated development, its direct MRT connectivity, ease of access to amenities, coupled with luxury finishes and facilities, helped strengthen its overall appeal to investors and owner-occupiers,” Seah says.

title: The Robertson Opus cultivates an urban oasis for luxury homes, dining and placemaking in District 9
article:
For years, Robertson Walk was a familiar dining and lifestyle destination along the Singapore River.

Now, The Robertson Opus is taking shape in its place, bringing new homes, retail offerings and landscaped public spaces to the Robertson Quay precinct in prime District 9.

Developed by Frasers Property and Sekisui House, the 999-year leasehold, mixed-use project will occupy the site of the former Robertson Walk commercial complex and the adjoining Fraser Place Robertson Walk serviced residence.

It will introduce 348 homes across five residential blocks arranged around a distinctive courtyard with publicly accessible spaces, alongside a retail podium that will retain the name Robertson Walk.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The project’s design also pays homage to the site’s heritage and the neighbourhood’s riverside character.

Its integration of residential, retail and communal spaces, with an emphasis on placemaking and sustainability, has earned it the Top Development title at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026.

“Our vision for The Robertson Opus was to deliver a distinctive riverside destination that combines quality homes, curated lifestyle offerings and meaningful communal spaces in one integrated environment,” says Tan Wee Hsien, CEO of Frasers Property Singapore.

He adds that the mixed-use project aims to enhance Robertson Quay’s vibrancy and create spaces “where people can live, connect and thrive”.

Prime riverside living with lasting appeal

Nestled between Fort Canning Hill and the Singapore River, The Robertson Opus is within walking distance of Robertson Quay’s restaurants, cafés and entertainment offerings.

Fort Canning, Clarke Quay and Great World MRT stations are nearby, while the Central Expressway provides road connectivity. Orchard Road and the CBD are also a short drive away.

Many buyers have been drawn to the 999-year leasehold tenure, prime riverside location and integrated lifestyle offerings.

“We have also seen interest from those seeking a legacy asset with generational appeal, as well as owner-occupiers who value the blend of city-centre convenience, wellness-focused amenities and proximity to the Singapore River’s vibrant lifestyle precinct,” Tan says.

Since its July 2025 debut, the project has attracted predominantly affluent Singaporeans, as well as permanent residents and a small number of international buyers.

The developers achieved a 41% take-up rate during the launch weekend, with 143 residential units sold at $3,360 psf on average. As at end-September 2026, about 60% of the residences had been sold.

“Homebuyers increasingly value developments that support their lifestyle, well-being and sense of belonging,” Tan notes.

Lively, connected community

The redevelopment presented an opportunity to reimagine the site while retaining the qualities that make the precinct unique.

Balancing renewal with respect for Robertson Quay’s character was a key consideration, Tan says.

The design thus prioritises openness, greenery and human-centric spaces. In terms of the architecture, modern facade compositions are harmonised with terracotta roof tiles and immersive landscaping.

Given the broader precinct’s history as a bustling waterfront trading corridor and gathering place, the developers applied a landscape framework that encourages interaction, connectivity and community engagement.

“Successful mixed-use developments are ultimately about placemaking,” Tan says.

“At The Robertson Opus, every component has been designed to complement one another while serving the needs of different user groups.”

Communal spaces are created to foster human connections and intergenerational engagement within a high-density urban environment. These include the Family Lawn, Gourmet Pavilion, Poolside Lounge, Reading Room, Children Sensory Garden and garden pavilions.

The project will also feature Singapore’s first sunken, privately owned public space, anchored by a three-storey green wall and water feature.

At the same time, the public-facing retail and dining promenade, along with strategically positioned internal public streets, contributes to the precinct’s vibrancy by extending the pedestrian experience.

This connects the development, riverfront and the surrounding neighbourhood, thereby merging the public and private realms.

The project will reintroduce Robertson Walk as an upscale destination with approximately 26 dining, retail and lifestyle units — catering to residents, visitors and the wider community.

“These complementary uses will foster a lively and engaging atmosphere, creating opportunities for meaningful social interaction and reinforcing Robertson Quay’s position as one of Singapore’s most sought-after lifestyle destinations,” Tan says.

Greenery, wellness and tranquillity

Extensive landscaping connects the residential blocks, elevated communal areas and retail podium.

The porous arrangement of the towers and the vertical internal courtyard — with cascading terraces, planted balconies and communal decks — draws breezes from the river deep into the development while mitigating heat build-up in the internal spaces.

Dense planting and water features also enable evaporative cooling and shading. More than 200 trees and 2,000 shrubs — comprising 40 to 50 native and regional species, including endangered trees — will be planted across the grounds.

Residents will benefit from a wellness-focused living environment that includes the rooftop Sky Forest with a 240m connected track across the blocks, as well as community gardening plots. Other amenities include a 45m lap pool, gym, sauna and social lounge.

“Together, these spaces support wellness, relaxation and social interaction while preserving the privacy and tranquillity of the residential experience,” Tan says.

The Robertson Opus has received BCA Green Mark GoldPlus certification. Sustainability measures include a climate-responsive design, naturally ventilated lobbies, low-volatile organic compound materials to improve indoor air quality, and rooftop solar photovoltaic panels.

Most of the existing carpark structure will be retained, while clay roof tiles and selected artefacts from the former development will be upcycled into an art wall at Level 1, preserving a link to the site’s past.

Meanwhile, the homes feature layouts that maximise usable space and natural ventilation.

Smaller unit types have ceiling heights of up to 3.2m, with built-in cabinetry making use of the additional height for storage. Strategically positioned windows encourage airflow, particularly in kitchens and bathrooms.

The unit interiors feature earthy tones and large-format tiles, and selected residences come with products from premium European brands such as Ernestomeda, Rimadesio and V-Zug.

With its rare 999-year tenure, luxury residences, tropical greenery and curated lifestyle offerings, The Robertson Opus brings together riverside living, wellness and community in the heart of District 9.

title: Newport Residences wins with elevated homes in a landmark CBD mixed-use development
article:
Newport Residences , City Developments Ltd ’s (CDL) ultra-luxury development on Anson Road in the CBD, launched for sale at the start of this year. The freehold project saw a healthy response, with buyers snapping up 57% of its 246 units during the Jan 31-Feb 1 launch weekend at an average price of $3,370 psf.

The robust performance reflected buyers’ anticipation for the project, which had been building up for some time. Newport Residences’ launch, originally scheduled for 2023, was postponed after the government raised additional buyer’s stamp duty (ABSD) rates as part of measures to cool the property market.

The ABSD hike, which kicked in near the end of April 2023, saw rates for foreigners — historically significant contributors to prime private home sales — double from 30% to 60%. Following the hike, foreign purchases of homes in the Core Central Region (CCR), typically seen as a proxy for luxury residences, took a hit, dampening the region’s sales.

CDL’s decision to delay the launch of Newport Residences until 2026 has proven to be judicious, following a notable recovery in the CCR market over the past year. Post-launch, the project has continued to see steady sales, with caveats lodged to date indicating a take-up rate of roughly 80%.

The development also swept multiple honours at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026. At the awards ceremony on Oct 29, the project walked away with four titles: Design Excellence, Innovation Excellence, Marketing Excellence and Top Development.

Landmark mixed-use development

Newport Residences is part of Newport Plaza, a mixed-use development on the site of the former Fuji Xerox Towers office complex. Standing at 215m, the 45-storey Newport Plaza also houses Newport Tower, a collection of Grade A offices on Levels 2 to 9, and branded serviced apartments on Levels 10 to 22.

Newport Residences makes up the upper half of the tower, from Levels 23 to 45. Restaurants and a public square on Level 1 round out the tower’s offerings.

Currently under construction, Newport Plaza is set to become a striking centrepiece in downtown Singapore. The development’s components, stacked within a single skyscraper, create a “vertical town” that combines work, live and play functions in a cohesive environment, according to the development’s EPEA entry submission.

Newport Plaza will be connected to the newly opened Prince Edward MRT Station on the Circle Line via a link bridge. It is also within walking distance of the Tanjong Pagar (East-West Line) and Cantonment (Circle Line) MRT stations.

Located in District 2 at the edge of the CBD, Newport Plaza is the first freehold mixed-use project developed under URA’s CBD Incentive Scheme, which encourages the conversion of older office buildings into mixed-use developments within the CBD.

Through the scheme, the site’s plot ratio was increased, along with a 25% uplift in gross floor area to about 655,000 sq ft.

‘Urban hill’

Judges for the EPEA 2026 were impressed by the thoughtful integration of Newport Plaza’s various uses. “Balancing so many different components in a single tower is a complicated task — one that the design team manages deftly,” says Mark Ong, group director at architectural and engineering firm P&T Consultants, who sat on the judging panel this year.

Newport Plaza was designed by Japanese practice Nikken Sekkei, in collaboration with local firm ADDP Architects.

Based in Tokyo, Nikken Sekkei is a historic firm best known for designing iconic structures such as the Tokyo Skytree broadcasting and observation tower and the Tokyo Dome indoor stadium. It is also known for its extensive experience in innovative urban design, having worked on local and international projects that range from cutting-edge skyscrapers to large-scale regeneration projects.

For Newport Plaza, Nikken Sekkei’s design was inspired by the concept of an “urban hill”, according to CDL. Using biophilic design principles, the Japanese firm conceived the tower’s distinct design, featuring cascading green terraces that curve along the lower floors occupied by the offices.

More greenery is woven throughout the building through multiple sky gardens, landscaped amenity decks and a roof garden. These collectively create a “green ribbon” that visually spirals up the tower.

EPEA judge Ong commends the development’s effective use of landscaping to delineate the tower’s different uses. For example, a sky terrace at Level 10 separates the offices from the serviced apartments, while another sky terrace at Level 22 acts as a divider between the serviced apartments and residences.

The softscaped open areas at the terraces provide physical partitions between the tower’s sections, while also ensuring users of each component have “their own green spaces”, Ong points out.

Newport Plaza is the second project Nikken Sekkei has designed for CDL. The  firm also worked on Zyon Grand , a 706-unit condo by CDL and Mitsui

Fudosan on Kim Seng Road. The 99-year leasehold project also garnered multiple wins at this year’s EPEA.

Premium living experience

Newport Residences was designed to set a new benchmark for city living. Located on the tower’s higher floors, the units enjoy unblocked panoramic views of the sea and city skyline.

Apartments range from one-bedroom units starting from 431 sq ft to four-bedroom premium units of 2,067 sq ft. There is also a super penthouse on the 45th floor. Spanning 12,060 sq ft, the lavish residence includes a dedicated lift and two private carpark lots.

All units feature elegant interiors, with marble flooring in the living spaces and glass balustrades at the balconies for uninterrupted views. The living area is equipped with a Haiku-branded fan, while a grille at the main entrance allows residents to keep the door open, promoting natural airflow.

The homes come with Liebherr and V-Zug kitchen appliances, along with bathroom fittings from Dornbracht and Duravit. Larger units include additional appliances such as steamers, wine chillers and dishwashers.

The apartments also feature a smart home setup that enables devices including air conditioners, doorbells, lighting and digital locksets to be remotely controlled.

Ample facilities across multiple levels

Residents will have access to a comprehensive range of facilities, which are dispersed across six levels.

A major highlight is Newport Sky, which crowns the 45-storey tower. The roof garden takes up the entire top floor, offering residents 360-degree scenic vistas. It also features resort-style amenities including four swimming pools, a pool deck and outdoor shower, a lounge, spaces for entertaining and a concierge desk.

A full-floor amenities deck at Level 34, known as Club Vista, serves as another hub for socialising and gathering. It includes a gym, co-working area and urban farming garden, alongside gourmet and social lounges.

More amenities are available at smaller sky gardens on Levels 25, 29, 37 and 41. These include an outdoor fitness station, a playground, a yoga area and an additional co-working lounge.

All the shared spaces feature lush greenery designed by Ecoplan Asia, the project’s landscape architect.

Recalibrating strategy

Newport Residences’ Marketing Excellence title at the EPEA is special recognition for the marketing efforts for the project.

The postponed sales launch meant that the project’s marketing had to undergo a “strategic recalibration”, according to the developer. Pre-marketing activities began in early November 2025, ahead of the project’s preview and sales launch in January 2026.

Animated EDMs (electronic direct mail) were used to tease the upcoming debut, while a multi-pronged marketing strategy using print, digital and broadcast media was deployed to further build awareness and communicate the project’s key features.

To showcase the homes and Newport Residences’ facilities, the developer rolled out virtual tours, 3D floorplans and detailed renderings, which were also made available on the project’s website.

For the super penthouse, CDL went the extra mile by creating a “spacewalk” virtual tour with interactive displays within a dedicated zone at the sales gallery, allowing for a hyper-immersive experience of the luxurious residence.

The rest of the sales gallery exhibits the same attention to detail. Visitors are greeted by a reception area that leads to a soaring model of Newport Plaza. Standing about 5m tall, it serves as a focal point that reinforces the project’s scale and positioning.

A smaller secondary model, along with comprehensive mock-ups of Newport Sky and Club Vista, lets visitors see the homes and amenities more closely.  In addition, the gallery houses the showflats for the two-bedroom premium and four-bedroom premium units.

title: Lentor Modern earns dual honours for homes rooted in nature and heritage
article:
The first and only integrated development in the immediate Lentor area, Lentor Modern brings together urban convenience and a design that pays tribute to the site’s natural heritage.

The residential component — comprising 605 homes spread across three 25-storey towers — obtained its temporary occupation permit at the end of August 2025.

Beneath the residential towers is a 96,000 sq ft commercial podium housing an integrated retail mall, which opened in January this year and is directly accessible to residents by lift.

Anchor tenants at the suburban mall include Cold Storage Fresh and Mulberry Learning pre-school, alongside a range of lifestyle, dining and essential-service options.

Lentor Modern is integrated with Lentor MRT Station, giving residents direct access to destinations such as Orchard Road, the Singapore Botanic Gardens, the CBD, Marina Bay and Gardens by the Bay.

The 99-year leasehold development by GuocoLand was the first to launch in the Lentor Hills estate. It drew a strong response, with an 84% take-up rate during its September 2022 launch weekend. It sold out in less than 2.5 years, with the last available unit sold in January 2025.

At the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026, the completed development clinched two accolades: Landscape Excellence, which recognises its strong emphasis on nature; as well as Top Development.

Integrating nature into design

Designed by ADDP Architects, Lentor Modern pays homage to the site’s heritage as a secondary forest. Nature-inspired prints adorn the retail podium’s façade, while abundant foliage and trees frame the development.

Above the podium, three residential towers rise from a landscaped deck, where a 200m meandering water feature recalls the Lentor stream that once flowed through the area.

The towers’ façades feature contrasting earth tones that complement the landscaping below.

Water and greenery are woven into the development’s recreational spaces, which include a 50m lap pool, 25m leisure pool, spa pool and jacuzzi alcove. Designed by landscape architecture firm Ortus Design, the landscape incorporates 150 species of native plants across the development.

Beyond the pools, the nature-inspired facilities include garden pavilions, a grand lawn, a glamping terrace, a full-size tennis court and a mini golf course.

The emphasis on nature continues upwards, with each residential tower featuring its own sky terrace. The verdant spaces offer sweeping views of Lower Seletar Reservoir and the surrounding landed housing enclave.

“As a condo located in the historic Lentor area, the project has done a good job of creating an ambience that feels natural,” says Ng Sze Oun, director of landscape studio Compound Collaborative and an EPEA 2026 judge.

The development is also close to nature and recreational amenities, including the future Lentor Hillock Park, Lower Peirce Reservoir Park, Thomson Nature Park and Bishan-Ang Mo Kio Park, with park connectors and cycling paths linking the surrounding green spaces.

Modern, comfortable homes

Practicality and long-term liveability underpin the design of Lentor Modern’s homes, which span one- to four-bedroom layouts measuring between 527 and 1,528 sq ft. These cater to diverse household needs, from young professionals to multigenerational families.

A flex room is included in the two- to four-bedders, offering homeowners a versatile space that can be used as a study, hobby room, nursery, wardrobe extension or storeroom as their needs change. Most flex rooms come with windows for natural airflow.

Everyday comfort is prioritised throughout the apartments. Windows are incorporated into the kitchens and both the master and common bathrooms, keeping spaces well-ventilated, naturally lit and comfortable for daily use.

Convenience is also built into the homes, with each unit equipped with a wireless smart home gateway system for remote control of lighting and air conditioning.

Anchoring Lentor’s transformation

Lentor Modern kickstarted the transformation of the Lentor Hills estate and anchors the new residential precinct.

The estate has seen the introduction of several other residential projects following Lentor Modern’s launch in 2022.

These include a number of GuocoLand-linked projects, such as Lentor Hills Residences , a 598-unit development launched in July 2023; and the 533-unit Lentor Mansion , which followed in March 2024.

Lentor Central Residences , a 477-unit project developed by a consortium comprising Hong Leong Holdings , GuocoLand and CSC Land , was launched in March 2025.

More recently, a GuocoLand-led consortium set a new benchmark for land rates in Lentor. In March, the consortium was awarded a Government Land Sale plot at Lentor Central for $657.1 million, or nearly $1,278 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr). GuocoLand intends to develop the site into three residential towers with up to 562 units.

The land rate beats the previous high of $1,204 psf ppr that GuocoLand paid for Lentor Modern’s site in 2021.

title: Vela Bay charts the course for Bayshore's seafront homes with coastal vistas, yacht-inspired design
article:
Bayshore is a new residential neighbourhood still taking shape along Singapore’s eastern coast.

Yet Vela Bay , the first private residential launch in the precinct, has set out to show what a new standard of seafront living in Singapore’s east could look like.

As the inaugural development in an emerging precinct, it had a unique opportunity to shape the district’s identity.

That vision guided every part of the project, from its nautical-inspired architecture to a resort-like setting that embraces the coast.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The result earned it the Top Development title at this year’s EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) and made it Bayshore’s first waterfront showpiece.

SingHaiyi Group Ltd and Chuan Capital jointly developed the 515-unit luxury project along Bayshore Walk, launching it in April 2026.

It is a rare offering in Singapore’s housing market, pairing the tranquillity of coastal living with convenient access to the city and established schools.

A strong start

Buyers responded quickly. Nearly 8,000 people visited over the preview weekend, and the project drew about 1,000 expressions of interest ahead of the launch. By the end of the launch weekend, 371 units, or 72% of the development, had been sold.

SingHaiyi put this partly down to pent-up demand. New private launches in the immediate East Coast area have been relatively limited, and the last major one nearby was Seaside Residences in 2017.

Interest came from investors, HDB upgraders and right-sizers, as well as families hoping to live closer to their loved ones.

Today’s buyers are also more discerning and look beyond location to connectivity, layouts and the overall quality of the living environment, SingHaiyi says.

Entering an emerging residential precinct as a first mover was a calculated decision.

The East Coast is already a well-established and highly sought-after residential neighbourhood, close to East Coast Park , reputable schools and lifestyle amenities, while Bayshore MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line links it directly to the city.

Rather than simply being the first to enter the market, the developers wanted Vela Bay to establish a benchmark for architectural excellence, thoughtful design and quality living that would remain relevant as the wider Bayshore community takes shape.

Designed around coastal living

More than 70% of the homes are sea-facing, with selected units enjoying uninterrupted views towards the coastline.

Working with architect P&T Consultants, the developers studied the site’s orientation to capture those views while keeping privacy, natural ventilation, solar exposure and residential density in balance. The towers are positioned so that many units avoid the harsh afternoon sun from the west.

One of the key challenges was the site’s proximity to underground MRT infrastructure and railway reserves, which constrained where buildings and facilities could go.

To work around this, the design team created an elevated bermed landscape deck that integrates essential infrastructure and servicing areas into the terrain, so residents get a raised, resort-like level set apart from the street below.

In Latin, vela means “sail”, and the condo’s design thus takes its cues from the elegance of luxury yachts gliding over calm waters and the movement of the sea.

The two towers are drawn in sleek horizontal lines, while their curved balcony edges and façade detailing recall the rhythm of ocean waves.

Sculpted rooftop crowns form a distinctive architectural silhouette and are expected to make the development a recognisable landmark along the East Coast Parkway.

At the heart of the landscape is the Vela Pavilion, a striking sail-inspired tensile canopy that serves as a focal point for the development. It is complemented by a swimming pool designed to resemble the bow of a yacht.

Inside, Singapore-based interior design studio Sujonohun created two schemes inspired by the Mediterranean Riviera.

Most units follow the “ Portofino ” concept, styled after sun-drenched seafront homes, with earthy tones and warm timber set against textured stone-look finishes.

The private lift units and penthouses use “Monaco”, a cooler palette of misty greys and ocean blues with metallic accents and refined stone textures for a sophisticated look. These larger homes also come with higher specifications, including gunmetal-finished fittings in selected bathrooms, integrated wine chillers and upgraded kitchen appliances.

Vela Bay’s units range from 484 sq ft one-bedroom-plus-study apartments to 1,582 sq ft, five-bedroom homes, along with two penthouses of 1,765 sq ft each. Two- and three-bedders make up the bulk, while larger units cater to multigenerational families.

A neighbourhood in the making

Much of Vela Bay’s long-term appeal rests on what Bayshore will become.

SingHaiyi sees it poised to emerge as one of Singapore’s most exciting new waterfront residential neighbourhoods, supported by a comprehensive master plan that brings together homes, green spaces, transport infrastructure and community amenities.

The precinct is planned as a car-lite neighbourhood with pedestrian-friendly streets and cycling paths.

The Thomson-East Coast Line is set to extend towards Changi Airport, and a mixed-use development integrated with Bedok South MRT Station and a bus interchange is on the way, along with a new Safra Bayshore clubhouse.

The developers have taken a similarly long-term approach at Vela Bay, where sustainability and adaptability are central to the design.

The development is designed to achieve BCA Green Mark Platinum Super Low Energy certification, complemented by energy-efficient features, solar panels and building design strategies aimed at reducing environmental impact.

Its vision of urban coastal living centres on seamlessly integrating work, family, wellness and recreation into everyday life.

A resident might begin the morning with a run or cycle along East Coast Park before taking the MRT to the CBD or Marina Bay for work, then return in the evening to unwind by the yacht-inspired pool.

Weekends bring opportunities to explore the Park Connector Network and Round Island Route, with more sports and recreational facilities to come at the future Safra Bayshore clubhouse.

The ultimate objective, SingHaiyi says, is a living environment where residents do not have to choose between the convenience of city life and the restorative qualities of nature.

title: The Sen scores with award-winning design centred around wellness
article:
The site of The Sen , a 347-unit residential development in District 21, offers something rare amid Singapore’s urban setting: a sense of calm, rooted in its proximity to nature.

Located along Jalan Jurong Kechil, off Upper Bukit Timah Road , the plot is a stone’s throw from Bukit Batok Nature Park and close to Bukit Timah Nature Reserve. Other parks, such as the Rail Corridor and Rifle Range Nature Park, are also nearby.

The area’s verdant greenery has heavily influenced The Sen’s design. Drawing inspiration from the surrounding landscapes, the condo is centred around wellness principles and a connection to nature.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The result impressed judges of this year’s EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA), who conferred the development the Design Excellence title for residential non-Central projects.

The Sen is developed by Sustained Land in a joint venture with Ho Lee Group and Greatview Development. The 99-year leasehold condo occupies a 207,156 sq ft site that the partners purchased in 2024 through a Government Land Sale tender for $278.9 million, or $841 psf per plot ratio.

Seamless integration

AGA Architects was appointed to design the project. The Singapore-based practice has also collaborated with Sustained Land on previous developments, such as the 250-unit Tre Residences on Geylang East Avenue 1, the  144-unit Coastline Residences on Amber Road, and the 96-unit 3 Cuscaden on Cuscaden Walk.

With The Sen, AGA Architects had to take into account the site’s topography, which features undulating terrain.

While this could have posed a design challenge, the firm, together with landscape architect Ecoplan Asia, took advantage of the site’s natural qualities to develop the condo’s layout and configuration.

The bulk of The Sen’s facilities lie at the heart of the site, tucked centrally among the development’s five residential blocks. They are spread across two main levels: Level 1 includes the drop-off area and the clubhouse, while Level 2 features the main pool deck with a 50m lap pool.

Meanwhile, the landscaping incorporates cascading terraces and tiered plantings that provide a fluid transition between the various spaces.

A wide variety of plants and trees, coupled with water features and sculptural elements, further blur boundaries while also giving the development a resort-like feel.

The seamless integration of all of The Sen’s components stood out to Mark Ong, group director of architectural and engineering firm P&T Consultants and one of the EPEA 2026 judges.

“What was impressive about The Sen is how the design makes you ‘forget’ about the challenge posed by the site’s topography,” he says. “The project effectively weaves together amenities and other facilities while navigating the site’s different levels with ease.”

Designed for well-being

The Sen’s residential towers each span 10 storeys, with the blocks strategically oriented to maximise light and ventilation.

Their façades’ finishes emulate wood and stone, complementing the greenery of the landscaping and surrounding nature reserves.

The earthy tones were deliberately paired with the development’s multiple pools to create a tranquil environment that promotes well-being.

The philosophy extends to The Sen’s residences, which prioritise both form and function to optimise day-to-day living.

Each unit features full-length windows and a private balcony. Coupled with an open-plan layout, these allow the homes to receive ample daylight and natural airflow, which offer benefits for both physical and mental health.

Interior finishes utilise different materials, such as engineered timber flooring and large- format tiles, to offer a clean, timeless aesthetic.

Units at The Sen are categorised into Classic and Prestige. The Classic homes, which span three of the five residential blocks, comprise one- to three-bedders ranging from 452 to 1,109 sq ft.

The remaining two blocks house Prestige homes, which consist of larger three-bedroom-plus-study and four-bedroom-plus-study units measuring between 1,259 and 1,453 sq ft.

Elevating everyday living

Facilities at The Sen were curated for a holistic lifestyle, with a variety of spaces for activity, relaxation and socialising.

In addition to the 50m lap pool, residents have access to a family pool, children’s pool, tennis court, gym, steam room, and hot and cold bath.

Lounge rooms and a barbecue pavilion provide spaces for gatherings, while family-friendly amenities include a playground, a play pavilion and several open lawns. In addition, there is a childcare centre on-site, located near the entrance with its own drop-off point.

More facilities are available at three sky terraces located at the Classic blocks. The landscaped communal spaces include dedicated yoga and Pilates areas, gardens and additional spaces for entertaining.

Beyond the lifestyle amenities, The Sen integrates green features that promote sustainability and an eco -conscious lifestyle.

Solar panels on the roof will generate electricity for common areas, while each home will come with a ceiling fan in the living room, reducing reliance on air conditioning. There will also be electric- vehicle charging stations at the car park, along with bicycle facilities.

The Sen was launched for sale in November 2025, with the developers moving about 23% of its units during the launch weekend at an average price of $2,358 psf.

Caveats lodged as at Oct 15 show that over half of the apartments have been taken up.

title: Boutique hotel on Hongkong Street for sale at $32 mil
article:
A boutique hotel housed in a conservation shophouse at 41 Hongkong Street is up for sale via an expression of interest (EOI) exercise. The 30-room property has a guide price of $32 million.

The shophouse is a five-storey conserved property with a six-storey rear extension on a 2,072 sq ft commercial site. The hotel — Luma41 – has 30 rooms on Levels 2 to 6, while the ground floor is occupied by Peranakan restaurant City PeraMakan.

The hotel has “80% to 90% occupancy”, according to Steward Asia (a unit of PropNex), which is marketing the property. It has also recently secured a permanent hotel license.

The shophouse has a total built-up area of approximately 8,872 sq ft, including the ground-floor F&B space of 1,051 sq ft. Based on the total built up area, the guide price works out to $3,607 psf.

Excluding the F&B component, the price for the hotel works out to “below $1 million per key”, adds Steward Asia.

The lease on the land has been topped up to a fresh 99 years from December 2018, while renovations costing $6 million have been carried out on the property, including the installation of a lift. The works were completed in 2019.

The property is a five-minute walk from Clarke Quay MRT Station.

Previously, the shophouse at 41 Hongkong Street was put up for sale for $35 million in 2023 . At the time, the hotel operated under the name Hotel Nuve Elements.

“Hotel licences in shophouses are hard to come by, and permanent ones even more so,” says Loyalle Chin, co-founder of Steward Asia. “41 Hongkong Street lets an investor step into a running hotel with its own F&B frontage, in a river precinct the government is actively revitalising.”

“With a permanent hotel licence, established operations and a prime location a short walk from Clarke Quay MRT Station, 41 Hongkong Street offers investors a rare combination of hospitality and F&B income at an attractive entry point,” adds Raelyn Lee, listing manager of Steward Asia.

The EOI closes at 3pm on Nov 27.

title: Springleaf Residence bridges heritage and nature in seamless harmony
article:
The launch of Springleaf Residence , the first high-rise condo in the Springleaf area, in August 2025 marked the first step in the transformation of the emerging precinct.

The 99-year leasehold development sits on a 344,700 sq ft site along Upper Thomson Road. GuocoLand and Hong Leong Holdings clinched the site through a Government Land Sale tender in April 2024 with the sole bid of $779.6 million, or $905 psf per plot ratio (psf ppr).

While the land parcel had attracted a measured response from developers, the project that followed drew strong interest from homebuyers. After a preview that attracted large crowds, Springleaf Residence sold 870 units (92%) within the first two days of its launch, at an average price of $2,175 psf.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

The robust performance reflected buyers’ confidence in the area’s growth potential, in line with URA’s vision for Springleaf as a vibrant precinct that combines urban living with natural spaces.

Since its launch, the development, which is under construction, has maintained steady sales, with lodged caveats indicating a take-up rate of close to 99% to date.

Springleaf Residence emerged as one of the standout winners at this year’s EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA), where it received four titles: Landscape Excellence, Innovation Excellence, Top Development and Top Selling Project in the Outside Central Region.

Reimagining heritage

Targeted for completion in 2029, the condo’s 941 homes are spread across five 25-storey residential towers and a conserved building — the former Upper Thomson Secondary School that was built in 1965.

Brick-like textures on the façades of the residential towers reference the architectural language of the conserved school building.

Desmond Sim, former group CEO of Realion Group and an EPEA judge, commended the project’s adaptive reuse of the heritage building, which will be converted into a low-rise block housing 32 apartments.

It will also include a dedicated wing for community activities, with facilities that are reminiscent of the building’s past as an educational institution, including a gym, a study room and an arts and crafts room.

Sim adds that the conversion of the heritage property offers residents distinctive homes, with conserved exteriors complemented by modern interiors.

The repurposed building fronts a lawn designed to resemble a school field, complete with a jogging track. Opposite it is the ECA House — a facility inspired by the extra-curricular activities once held in schools — which houses a kitchen, multi-purpose rooms and outdoor dining pavilions.

Nature-conscious design

The EPEA 2026 judges were also impressed by the project’s thoughtful design that responds to its natural setting, with Springleaf Forest and the Central Catchment Nature Reserve nearby.

“The developers have placed a strong focus on the site and taken the existing natural environment into consideration,” says Ng Sze Oun, director of landscape studio Compound Collaborative and a member of the judging panel.

The development was designed by ADDP Architects, with landscaping by Ortus Design. The project team also included biodiversity specialist Camphora, which provided input on the ecological design.

Guided by the concept of “Forest in a Home, Home in a Forest”, the development adopts a biodiversity-sensitive approach, with residential spaces that coexist with the natural environment.

The key features are a 730m native forest corridor and a 240m native forest belt that encircle the development. Featuring lush plantings that include native species from Springleaf Forest, they serve as an extension of the surrounding forest strip.

Microhabitats will be integrated throughout the project, including on the roofs of the ECA House and pavilions, which will also feature native tree species. Elevated above areas of human activity, these green roofs support birds, pollinators and other wildlife, enriching the landscaping’s ecological value.

Other measures were incorporated specifically with the welfare of wildlife in mind. These include façade windows with a window-to-wall percentage below 50% and recessed glazing to reduce reflectivity and mitigate bird strikes, as well as smooth-finish perimeter walls and cantilevered aprons to deter long-tailed macaques from entering residential areas.

Ng commends the development for its efforts to incorporate biodiversity into its design. “Springleaf Residence sets a good example for other landscape architects to consider similar approaches to designing spaces that coexist with nature,” Ng says.

Wellness-focused facilities

A range of facilities supporting recreation, wellness and an appreciation of nature are spread across the development.

Water-based amenities include a 50m lap pool, spa pool, hydrotherapy pool, leisure pool and wading pool, catering to residents of different ages and preferences.

Cocoon-shaped pavilions of varying sizes provide spaces for yoga and relaxation, pet play, dining and social gatherings.

Facilities such as the Forest Boardwalk, Rain Garden and Bio Pond bring the surrounding natural environment into residents’ daily lives.

The development also takes an educational approach to nature, with an outdoor classroom featuring a variety of plant species as well as interactive signage on local flora and fauna.

Modern, functional homes

Springleaf Residence’s homes come in a variety of layouts to serve a wide spectrum of homeowners.

The five residential towers will comprise two- to five-bedroom units, sized from 527 to 1,475 sq ft.

These units overlook the pool, landscaped grounds, or the surrounding Springleaf Forest and Central Catchment Nature Reserve.

Meanwhile, the 32-unit, low-rise conserved block will house one- to three-bedroom units, measuring between 388 and 1,259 sq ft.

Across all homes, the living rooms, dry kitchens and bedrooms will have wood-toned vinyl flooring, which lends the spaces a warm aesthetic while offering ease of maintenance and everyday comfort.

Bathrooms and wet kitchens are finished with anti-slip porcelain tiles for durability and water resistance.

The homes are equipped with a smart home system for residents to remotely control devices such as air-conditioning units, doorbells, lighting and digital locks. A smart electricity monitoring system is also provided to track each unit’s power consumption.

At the heart of an emerging precinct

Despite its forested surroundings, Springleaf Residence is just a two-minute sheltered walk from Springleaf MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL), which connects residents directly to destinations such as Orchard Road and the CBD. In the future, TEL will also connect to Changi Airport Terminal 5.

Springleaf Residence is part of an up-and-coming precinct that can accommodate about 2,000 homes when completed.

The precinct is gradually taking shape, with the strong sales momentum at Springleaf Residence inspiring renewed developer interest in the area.

A neighbouring land parcel along Upper Thomson Road attracted five bids when its second tender closed in October last year.

Wee Hur Holdings secured that 262,875 sq ft site after submitting the highest bid of $613.94 million, or $1,062 psf ppr. The site had previously been launched in December 2023, but attracted no bids when the tender closed in June 2024.

As the surrounding area evolves, Springleaf Residence is setting a noteworthy precedent for the neighbourhood with its rare combination of urban convenience, heritage character and close integration with nature.

title: Four CBD conservation shophouses for sale at $91.8 mil
article:

title: At Narra Residences in Dairy Farm, nature-centric living takes centre stage
article:
Narra Residences , a 540-unit condo along Dairy Farm Walk, has been named Top Development in the uncompleted residential (non-central) category at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards 2026.

Jointly developed by Santarli Realty, Apex Asia Development , Soon Li Heng Group and Kay Lim Realty, it draws inspiration from the natural surroundings of Dairy Farm and the broader Bukit

Timah belt, incorporating elements of the area’s forests, reservoirs and quarries into its architecture and landscaping.

Get the latest details on available units and prices for Narra Residences

Designed by P&T Consultants, Narra Residences is envisioned as a “forest retreat”, blending contemporary architecture with abundant greenery and landscaped communal spaces.

The development comprises residential blocks ranging from six to 16 storeys, arranged to complement the surrounding terrain.

A key feature is the generous spacing between the blocks, reaching up to 63m at its widest point. This enhances privacy and natural ventilation while creating a greater sense of openness.

“Narra Residences’ design was very much shaped by its location in Dairy Farm,” says Jocelyn Tan, CEO of Apex Asia Development. “We wanted to respond to this setting and create a development that feels connected to its environment rather than being separate from it.”

With 66% of the site dedicated to greenery and immersive landscaped expanses, nature is at the heart of its design.  The location also puts residents near more than 2,000ha of nature reserves and 20km of nature trails.

Cues from the quarry, forest and reservoir

The development’s architectural and landscape concepts take their cues from three defining elements of the Dairy Farm area: the quarry, forest and reservoir.

These influences are expressed through the material palette, architectural forms and landscape features.

Textures and tones inspired by natural stone reflect the rugged character of nearby quarries, while vertical architectural elements echo the surrounding forest greenery. Cascading water features and pools draw inspiration from the vicinity’s reservoirs.

The residential blocks are oriented to maximise natural daylight and ventilation while minimising exposure to the afternoon sun where possible.

Landscape architectural firm Ecoplan Asia translated the nature-inspired concept into a series of interconnected landscaped areas. Layered tropical planting, shaded walkways and garden pockets soften the built environment, creating a continuous green experience.

“The forest, reservoir and quarry became references for the different landscape zones and experiences within Narra Residences,” says Tan. “Each space has its own character, but they come together as part of one continuous journey through the development.”

The landscaping consists of a diverse selection of trees, shrubs and groundcover, with more than half of the plant palette comprising native Southeast Asian species. Pollinator-supportive planting also encourages biodiversity by providing habitats for birds, butterflies and beneficial insects.

Narra Residences has a green plot ratio of 5.02 and a landscape replacement area of 65%, reflecting the extent of greenery incorporated into the development.

That concept extends to the recreational facilities, where water features and landscaping evoke a resort-like atmosphere.

A 50m lap pool is framed by lush planting and landscaped decks, while the Family Canyon Pool offers a more informal setting with its organic contours inspired by natural landforms.

Other facilities include a tennis court, golf simulator, clubhouses, function rooms, barbecue pavilions and outdoor dining spaces.

A forest-themed playground, children’s pool and indoor playroom cater to younger residents, while landscaped gardens and pavilions provide nooks for relaxation and social interaction.

“The planning of the spaces, landscaping and amenities was approached as one connected experience,” says Tan, adding that the intention was to provide sections where people could exercise, relax, spend time with family or enjoy the surroundings.

Homes designed for everyday living

The nature-focused design continues within the residences, with interiors by Index Design featuring warm earth tones, soft greys and natural textures.

The light-toned finishes reflect natural daylight, creating bright living zones, while full-height wardrobes, integrated joinery and concealed storage solutions maximise usable space.

Narra Residences offers a range of configurations, from one-bedroom-plus-study units to five-bedroom apartments with private lifts, catering to different household needs.

The layouts emphasise spatial efficiency and flexibility, with regularly shaped rooms that can accommodate different furniture arrangements. Selected rooms can be adapted into home offices, guest rooms or hobby zones, while larger units have enclosed kitchens, spacious bedrooms and dedicated yards.

The development also has sustainability features, including rooftop solar photovoltaic panels to offset part of the electricity consumption in common areas, motion-sensor lighting in selected communal sections, and fittings that are water-efficient.

A pneumatic waste conveyance system facilitates waste collection through an enclosed vacuum-based network, improving cleanliness and operational efficiency. Naturally ventilated corridors, shaded communal areas and extensive landscaping contribute to thermal comfort.

Connectivity and convenience

Narra Residences offers access to transport links, schools and daily amenities.

The development includes four retail units. Dining and shopping options are also available at Dairy Farm Mall just across the road.

Families with school-going children benefit from the development’s proximity to schools. For instance, CHIJ Our Lady Queen of Peace and Bukit Panjang Primary School are within 1km. Two international schools, German European School Singapore and The Perse School (Singapore), are within walking distance.

Apex Asia’s Tan notes that the condo’s appeal lies in combining these conveniences with the vicinity’s natural character.

“Ultimately, we wanted Narra Residences to bring together the things that matter in everyday living — space, greenery, accessibility and convenience — while allowing residents to enjoy the distinctive natural character of Dairy Farm,” she says.

title: February 2027 BTO exercise to offer 4,300 flats in Bishan, Toa Payoh, Tampines and Tengah
article:
About 4,300 flats in Bishan, Toa Payoh, Tampines and Tengah will be launched for sale under the February 2027 Build-To-Order (BTO) exercise. In addition, about 5,000 flats will be offered for sale under a concurrent Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) exercise, said HDB.

The BTO exercise will be the smallest since February 2022, when 4,126 units were offered, says Lee Sze Teck, senior director of data analytics at Huttons Asia.

Over half of the units (around 2,210 units or 51.6%) will be from two projects located in Bishan and Toa Payoh, which he believes could potentially be Prime developments. That is a higher proportion than recent BTO exercises.

Split between Prime, Plus and Standard flats in past BTO exercises

The remaining flats are located across two projects in Tampines and one project in Tengah, which Lee expects will be Standard developments.

Bishan project to offer 1,070 flats

The Bishan project is projected to offer about 1,070 flats, comprising two-room flexi, three-room and four-room units.

“Demand may be robust given the project’s proximity to a number of popular schools like Catholic High School and Ai Tong School,” says Christine Sun, chief researcher and strategist at Realion (OrangeTee & ETC) Group.

While not situated near an MRT station, the site is close to amenities nearby such as Junction 8 mall, Bishan Park and Thomson Plaza .

Huttons’ Lee notes that Bishan flats have been “extremely popular”, going by past BTO exercises. Sin Ming Residences, launched in Dec 2023, saw an application rate above 3 for the 4-room flats among first-timers.

“The next two BTOs in Bishan, Bishan Terraces in October 2025 and Lakeview Cascadia in June 2026, continued to see sustained interest with an application rate above 3,” Lee adds.

Toa Payoh project next to Mount Pleasant MRT Station

The Toa Payoh project is expected to offer about 1,140 two-room flexi, three-room and four-room flats.

“This upcoming BTO project is likely to be popular, as it is next to the planned opening of Mount Pleasant MRT station on the Thomson-East Coast Line,” says Realion’s Sun. It is also near schools such as SJI International School and CHIJ Primary Toa Payoh.

This will be the second BTO in the Mount Pleasant precinct. It follows Mount Pleasant Crest,a Prime project that was “very popular” among buyers when it launched in October 2025, drawing 3.3 first-time applicants for the four-room flats, says Huttons’ Lee.

Tampines projects to include CCA, five-room flats

The two projects in Tampines comprise a site at the corner of Simei Road and Upper Changi Road , along with another at Tampines Street 11.

The Simei Road-Upper Changi Road site will offer 460 units, from two-room flexi to five-room flats. It is close to Upper Changi MRT Station (Downtown Line), while the Expo MRT Interchange (Downtown and East-West lines) is about 500m away, says Huttons’ Lee.

Realion’s Sun expects flats at the site — especially the five-room units — to be popular among buyers, based on past performance of nearby BTO Simei Symphony, launched in July 2025. “Following the healthy application rate of 8.9 for 4-room flats at Simei Symphony, we can expect strong interest in this project as well, especially given the low number of units,” she says.

The site at Tampines Street 11 will offer about 330 Community Care Apartments (CCAs) and four-room flats. It is about 500m away from Simei MRT Station on the East-West Line.

Some 240 units will be designated as CCAs, notes Sun. “As the first batch of CCAs to be offered in Tampines, the project could attract considerable interest from older residents in the area who are looking to right-size from their existing HDB flats and use the proceeds for retirement.”

Tengah project to be in newer Brickland precinct

The Tengah project is located in the relatively new Brickland precinct within the estate. It will offer 1,280 homes, ranging from two-room flexi to five-room flats.

The site is close to the future Brickland MRT Station on the North-South Line, slated to open around 2034. “In the future, there will be a mixed-use development next to it which will improve the amenities,” adds Huttons’ Lee/

title: UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard redefines luxury urban living
article:
When the tender for a Government Land Sale (GLS) site at Orchard Boulevard was launched in October 2023, market observers noted its significance.  In addition to being in the Core Central Region (CCR), where GLS sites are relatively limited due to supply constraints, it was the first GLS plot to launch for sale in the Orchard area since 2018.

Located close to the Orchard Road shopping belt, the 99-year leasehold site was zoned for residential use with commercial at the first storey. The plot’s appeal was underscored by its connectivity, with the site located right next to the Orchard Boulevard MRT Station on the Thomson-East Coast Line.

The site’s launch also came at an interesting time for CCR developments. A hike in additional buyer’s stamp duty rates — including a doubling of the rate applicable to foreigners to 60% — had taken effect in April that year, leading to a pullback in CCR sales volume.

Search for the latest New Launches , to find out the transaction prices and available units

Still, developers took a keen interest in the Orchard Boulevard plot. A joint venture between UOL Group and Singapore Land Group (SingLand) was eventually awarded the site in February 2024 after the partners submitted the top tender offer of 428.28million(1,616 psf per plot ratio).

The following year, the developers launched UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard : a 35-storey tower housing 301 luxury residences.

The District 10 development has garnered three titles at the EdgeProp Singapore Excellence Awards (EPEA) 2026. They are: Design Excellence (Luxury), Top Development and Top Luxury Development.

Irregular plot

A significant part of the success of UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard at EPEA 2026 relates to the project’s clever adaptation of its unique site attributes.

The land parcel has an irregular shape, comprising a main plot with a smaller triangular extension at the bottom right end. On the other end, the site abuts a piece of state land that developers were required to turn into a public park.

The project’s connection to an MRT station, along with its retail component, added to the complexity of creating a development that offered exclusivity and privacy for its residents.

Despite the challenges posed by the site’s “awkward shape” and its public-facing components, UOL and SingLand were able to turn these aspects into “key virtues” through thoughtful design, says Mark Ong, group director at P&T Consultants and an EPEA 2026 judge.

Creating a distinct offering

Designed by ADDP Architects, UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard features a sleek tower, with a tasteful façade that blends aluminium glazing, concrete surfaces and finely detailed lattice fins and panels. The car park and a landscaped facilities deck separate the street- level retail area and neighbouring public park from the residences, which begin on Level 2.

The small triangular plot extension, which may have appeared out of place initially, was reimagined as one of the condo’s unique offerings: The Botanical Villa. Positioned as a private wellness retreat nestled in greenery, the standalone structure features a massage room, a hydropool and an indoor spa pool.

Other facilities, located at the main landscaped deck, include a 50m infinity pool, leisure pool, gym, play area, lounges and a function room. Residents will also have access to concierge services.

“What I find particularly compelling about UpperHouse is how the developer turned an irregular, angular site into an opportunity to create a distinctive resort-style residential experience,” says Sky Seah, another EPEA 2026 judge. Seah is an academic director at the National University of Singapore.

Harmonious landscaping

Landscaping plays a big role in amplifying the development’s resort-like qualities. Ecoplan Asia, the project’s landscape architect, was tasked with creating an environment that reinforces biophilic principles, while also giving the development a sense of place.

Drawing inspiration from the nearby Singapore Botanic Gardens, Ecoplan Asia employed the use of lush, multi-layered greenery to create an immersive landscape. Diverse vegetation, including native and mature plantings, was chosen to help the architecture blend seamlessly with its surroundings.

The landscaping softens the transitions between the project and its public spaces, including the neighbouring park, which Ecoplan Asia also designed. Care was taken to ensure a sense of continuity in the landscape design, which helps to blur the boundaries between the public and private realms, and create a sense of openness.

Functional, luxurious homes

UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard’s residences feature a variety of layouts, divided between Signature and Bespoke homes.

The Signature collection consists of one-bedroom-plus-study to premium three-bedroom units, measuring from 474 to 1,012 sq ft. The Bespoke units, which take up one stack within the tower, comprise four-bedroom suites sized 2,056 sq ft.

The tower is oriented such that units face towards the park or the surrounding landed enclave. Units were also planned with a strong emphasis on efficiency and versatility, allowing residents to adapt the space according to their needs.

For instance, the two-bedroom units have a dumbbell layout to reduce wasted corridor space, along with a defined kitchen that can be enclosed if needed.

In the two-bedroom-plus-study apartments, the study is situated close to the master bedroom, allowing for its flexible use as a walk-in wardrobe or nursery.

Designed with families in mind, the three-bedroom units feature contiguous living and dining areas, along with a balcony that extends the living space.

In the four-bedroom suites, thoughtful features elevate the homes. These include double-volume living and dining spaces, wet and dry kitchens, and a private lift and car park lot.

Massone Ong did the interior design for the residences and common areas. The Singapore-based practice also designed the project’s sales gallery and four-bedroom show suite.

Top Luxury Development hat trick

UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard is the latest project under UOL’s Masterpiece Collection — a series of developments that it sees as setting new benchmarks for luxury homes in Singapore.

The collection began with Watten House , an 180-unit project on Shelford Road in District 11. The freehold, low-density development features expansive homes, starting from three-bedders.

The second Masterpiece Collection development was Meyer Blue , located along Meyer Road in District 15. The 226-unit freehold condo fronting East Coast Park was positioned as luxury coastal homes, offering unblocked sea views.

Both projects, jointly developed by UOL and SingLand, were past winners of EPEA’s Top Luxury Development award: Watten House scored the title in 2024, followed by Meyer Blue the following year.

With UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard claiming the title this year, UOL and SingLand have scored a rare EPEA hat trick, clinching the award three years in a row.

Meeting high-end buyers’ needs

The success of UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard follows a well-received launch last year.

The project hit the market following private previews in July 2025, during a busy weekend that coincided with two other project launches: the 348-unit, 999-year leasehold The Robertson Opus in Robertson Quay, and the 600-unit executive condo Otto Place in Tengah.

Against this backdrop, UpperHouse at Orchard Boulevard posted a strong performance, moving 53% of units at an average price of $3,350 psf during its launch weekend. The development is now over 80% sold, based on lodged caveats.

The healthy sales are a testament to the project’s distinct qualities, which resonate with today’s high-end property buyers, notes EPEA judge Seah.

“Beyond prime location and premium finishes, luxury buyers are increasingly interested in the overall living experience: privacy, wellness, thoughtful design, quality landscaping and amenities that support their lifestyles.”
