Spreads between AI and non-AI names in the US investment-grade market have diverged in recent months, according to calculations by LPL Financial.

The average cost of debt for tech giants has been increasing with almost every new dollar issue in the past two years. And rising government bond yields driven by lofty energy prices has been another pain point for the sector.

Hyperscaler supply is “more as a sector-specific technical challenge than a broader deterioration in credit fundamentals,” Adam Whiteley, head of global credit at Insight Investment, said in emailed comments.

title: US trade deficit narrows slightly on pickup in goods exports
article:
(Nov 4): The US trade deficit narrowed slightly in September as the value of goods exports rose to a four-month high.

The gap in goods and services trade shrank 0.7% from the prior month to US$105 billion ($134 billion), Commerce Department data showed Wednesday. Economists projected a US$107.9 billion shortfall, based on the median estimate in a Bloomberg survey.

The monthly trade figures, which are not adjusted for inflation, have gyrated through US tariffs, a war-driven jump in oil prices, supply-chain disruptions and surging demand for computers, semiconductors and other components needed to build more data centres.

The value of exports rose 1.9%, led by an increase in outbound shipments of capital goods. Imports increased 1.2%, also led by a surge in business equipment.

The value of inbound capital goods — a category that includes computers and accessories, semiconductors and telecommunications equipment — rose US$11.6 billion from a month earlier to a fresh record. US companies are spending heavily on imported technology to ramp up artificial intelligence capacity.

At the same time, imports of industrial supplies, which include oil and petroleum products, fell US$3.7 billion from a month earlier. The US imported fewer barrels of crude oil than a month earlier, according to the report. Exports of industrial supplies decreased US$1 billion.

See also: US job openings jump to four-month high, lay-offs decline

Imports and exports of nonmonetary gold, a category that has been volatile recently, also declined.

On an inflation-adjusted basis, the overall merchandise-trade deficit widened to US$119.5 billion in September, the largest since March 2025.

Exports of services, a category that includes travel, royalties and financial services, ticked up to a fresh record.

See also: Fed officials back more rate hikes, gradual pace of tightening

By country, the US merchandise trade deficit with Canada shrank. Companies on both sides of the border stepped up shipments this summer to get ahead of tariffs after trade talks fell apart. US tariffs of 50% took effect on billions of dollars of Canadian goods on Aug 22; Canada retaliated with levies of its own.

title: Singapore changes haze law to include arrests, heavier fines
article:
(Nov 4): Singapore has passed amendments to toughen its law on cross-border haze, responding to a devastating wildfire season in Indonesia that cloaked the city-state in smog for weeks.

Following an hours-long debate in Parliament on Wednesday, the country bolstered existing rules with measures including restrictions and fines for businesses dealing with entities or individuals suspected to have engaged in conduct leading to the blazes.

The changes allow for arrests in Singapore and boost the maximum fines for causing or contributing to haze-related fires from $100,000 per day to $1 million per day, with the cap increasing tenfold to $20 million.

“Following the recent haze episode, it is clear that the status quo is not tenable,” Sustainability and Environment Minister Grace Fu said in the Parliament session on Wednesday. “We need better ways to obtain and verify information, trace complex corporate relationships and impose meaningful consequences on errant entities, even where criminal prosecution proves difficult.”

Fires in Indonesia have spewed pollution across the region in recent months, sending air quality to “very unhealthy” levels at times in Singapore. The smog — which has also fuelled protests in Indonesia — has spread into Malaysia and the Philippines, closing schools and driving demand for air purifiers.

The enhanced legislation is Singapore’s latest effort to hold firms accountable for the seasonal fires, which are often linked to land clearing for agriculture. The issue has been worsened this year by a strong El Niño weather pattern that exacerbated and prolonged the dry season. Rains have recently picked up, improving air quality levels.

See also: Indonesia rain set to ease toxic haze in Singapore, Malaysia

The latest amendments allow for offences to be heard in court in the absence of an accused person, and expand the scope of the act to include conduct contributing to land and forest fires that pose a risk of haze pollution to Singapore — even before it reaches its shores.

While supporting the bill, lawmakers questioned the reach of the rejigged act, and whether companies linked to the fires would be allowed to raise money in Singapore’s capital markets. They also asked for Singapore to do more to stop forest fires at their source, and to try and mobilise more capital toward peat-land restoration and forest conservation.

“The punishments are not only monetary. The measures can be used to restrict and deny commercial activities and financing — effectively making the company a corporate pariah,” said Simon Tay, chairman of the Singapore Institute of International Affairs, an independent think tank. “There are nevertheless safeguards to ensure that prevention, proof and punishment will be administered justly in accordance with the rule of law.”

See also: RegCo issues additional queries to SGX-listed companies with links to haze

Singapore enacted its transboundary haze law in 2014, allowing the country to issue daily fines to polluting companies. The city-state tried to enforce that legislation during a severe haze episode in 2015, but conceded at the time it was having difficulty getting information from Indonesian authorities. Four cases remain under investigation.

“Three of the four entities investigated have also been identified in our investigations in the current haze episode. Their past actions will be considered as we investigate the current case,” Fu said in Parliament.

The government has recently stepped up efforts to pursue companies that may have contributed to this year’s pollution. The amendments allow for greater ability to conduct such investigations.

The National Environment Agency (NEA) has issued notices to a number of firms in Indonesia and separately sought information from 10 Singapore-registered palm oil and forestry companies, including Wilmar International Ltd, Golden Agri International Pte Ltd, and First Resources Ltd.

Senior government officials also met representatives of the Singapore-based companies issued notices by NEA, saying they would be expected to appoint independent assessors to examine their operations, supply chains and corporate relationships. Fu said last week the government would amend the haze law to give the framework legal force.

The number of hotspots detected in Indonesia in September and October were the highest since 2015, the forestry ministry’s SiPongi platform shows.

While advances in satellite imagery and modelling have improved authorities’ ability to trace smoke, Singapore still needs official information and records from host countries where the fires occur to pinpoint those responsible, Fu said in a parliament session on Tuesday.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

She added that Singapore has offered firefighting and cloud-seeding assistance, while stressing that any support must be coordinated with Jakarta. Indonesia informed Singapore last month that it was able to handle the fires and didn’t require foreign assistance, she said.

“We don’t want to offer help when they don’t need or impose ourselves,” Fu said, adding that Singapore would continue discussions with Indonesian counterparts on how it could complement their efforts.

The two countries signed an environmental cooperation agreement in June that includes transboundary pollution, while Singapore is also working through Asean toward the region’s goal of being haze-free by 2030 as it prepares to chair the association next year.

“Haze no longer has to reach Singapore. A risk of it reaching Singapore is enough,” said Khor Yu Leng, a senior economist at Segi Enam Advisors in Singapore.

title: Copper follows stock markets higher as democrats sweep congress
article:
(Nov 4): Copper climbed as stock markets turned higher and the dollar dropped after US midterm elections that saw the Democrats sweep Congress.

Benchmark three-month futures pared early losses to bounce back above US$14,000 a tonne in London, tracking a rebound in US equity futures after an initial selloff.

Democrats won control of both chambers in a result that will leave US President Donald Trump far more hemmed in than in the first two years of his second term, when Republican control of Congress left few checks on his power.

Copper has had a volatile year, touching a record high in September before easing in recent weeks, as concerns over spending on artificial intelligence hurt equities and fuelled fears about global growth. The initial rout in stock markets on Wednesday (Nov 4) came as investors questioned whether a Democratic Congress will impede the development of data centres and associated infrastructure.

Following the Democrats’ win, tighter scrutiny of the AI sector will continue to pressure copper despite short-term price swings, said Li Xuezhi, head of research at brokerage Chaos Ternary Futures Co.

See also: Copper, tin fall with base metals on renewed AI stocks selloff

After the US vote, traders will also be focused on Trump’s potential implementation of a tariff on refined-copper imports — a possibility that has drawn vast amounts of metal into the US.

The prospect of tariffs has driven up Comex copper futures over LME prices since Trump came to office, but in recent weeks the spread between the two contracts has narrowed as doubts grow about whether he will push ahead with the levies. The rise in the cost of living, partly associated with his import duties, was a major reason behind voter discontent.

The front-month Comex-LME spread initially traded at negative levels on Wednesday before rebounding to leave Comex trading at a premium of about US$100 a tonne by mid-morning in London.

See also: Copper recovers as easing tech rout, lower oil calm growth fears

Copper was 0.6% higher at US$14,116 a tonne on the London Metal Exchange as of 10.30am local time, after earlier losing as much as 1.5%. Nickel rallied 2%, leading all metals higher on the exchange.

title: Cyberattackers drain money from French bank Credit Mutuel Arkea
article:
(Nov 4): Crédit Mutuel Arkéa said hackers stole money from it after gaining access to its computer systems, underscoring the growing cybersecurity risks for the banking sector.

The French lender “was the victim of a cyberattack that enabled fraudulent transactions to be carried out”, a spokesperson confirmed to Bloomberg News on Wednesday (Nov 4), declining to say how much money was stolen.

The spokesperson said some transactions have been suspended and the bank is in contact with authorities about the attack. The situation is “under control", and there will not be a financial hit to clients.

It is the latest example of cyberattacks on banks around the world. The State Bank of India, the country’s largest lender by assets, recently launched a probe after a suspected cyberattack exposed thousands of customer records containing personal information. In Japan, a wave of data breaches has hit companies including Daiwa Securities Group Inc, East Japan Railway Co and SoftBank Corp, prompting government officials to step up cybersecurity measures.

Hackers also recently pulled off the biggest heist that the digital-asset industry has ever faced, draining more than US$6 billion from crypto exchange Binance.

Cyber risks are increasing “exponentially” and represent “the price to be paid for all this innovation", UBS Group AG CEO Sergio Ermotti said earlier this week. Good governance, clear accountability and the ability to react quickly in this environment are key, he added.

See also: Singtel, DART launch cyber training with simulated attacks on critical infrastructure networks

Crédit Mutuel Arkéa earlier this year filed an application to obtain a MiCA authorisation, the European regulation on crypto-assets, to offer crypto services to its customers.

title: India approves US$1.5 bil push for energy storage capacity
article:
(Nov 4): India will set aside INR145 billion in subsidies to help build 92GWh of energy storage capacity, seeking to make better use of its rapidly expanding renewable power fleet and transmission network, information minister Ashwini Vaishnaw told reporters in New Delhi on Wednesday (Nov 4).

The financial boost will run through 2031 and is designed to help companies in the storage sector kickstart operations as the nascent market takes off.

Currently, India’s storage capacity sits at about 54GWh but the government aims to reach 411GWh of storage capacity by the financial year 2031-32.

The decision seeks to address a growing structural challenge for India’s energy transition, as the country has been adding more solar and wind generation capacity than the grid is able to absorb. Solar and wind capacity has quadrupled since 2017 to about 230GW, accounting for 41% of the total installations. Billions of dollars have also been invested in transmission lines to carry renewable electricity across the country.

But much of that infrastructure cannot be fully utilised around the clock. Solar plants stop generating after sunset while during the day the grid can struggle to absorb all the electricity produced when solar output peaks.

The subsidies are meant to lead to a total investment of INR976 billion and will require companies applying for support to source at least 40% of their equipment in the country, encouraging domestic manufacturing.

See also: Singaporean plan to import clean power hits Indonesian hurdle

The cabinet also approved financial incentives worth over INR28 billion to bolster processing of critical minerals in the country, Vaishnaw said. The move will boost India’s manufacturing in sectors including electronics, semiconductors, batteries, defence and heavy equipment and will help the country reduce import dependence, she told reporters.

title: Thai spyware alerts prompt opposition leaders to demand probe
article:
(Nov 4): Two Thai opposition leaders are demanding the government disclose whether state agencies targeted political leaders with spyware ahead of a December no-confidence debate, days after Apple Inc software flagged attempted attacks on their phones.

Opposition leader Natthaphong Ruengpanyawut of the People’s Party and Democrat Party leader Abhisit Vejjajiva said at a joint press conference on Wednesday that they’d received mobile security alerts, raising questions over whether the alleged attempted intrusions may be linked to their scrutiny of the government.

Abhisit called on the government to confirm that no security agency or other state body was involved in the incidents, which triggered the phone alerts late in October.

The government has already denied targeting politicians with spyware, and Digital Economy and Society Minister Chaichanok Chidchob on Tuesday said that similar alerts were reported across 99 countries. He said authorities were seeking information from Apple Inc and planned to raise the issue at the National Security Council.

His deputy, Boonthida Somchai, said affected politicians had not yet submitted their alerts directly to the ministry for verification.

Former MP Wiroj Lakkhanaadisorn, an ex-chair of the House Armed Forces Committee, told Bloomberg that attempts to extract information from another person’s phone could constitute a criminal offence.

See also: Indonesia arrests ex-police chief for alleged wiretap of Prabowo

He argued that such surveillance would violate Thailand’s Personal Data Protection Act and called for answers from the government, including Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul in his capacity as head of the Internal Security Operations Command, citing past allegations involving the agency. ISOC is the internal security arm of the Thai armed forces.

The lawmakers’ questions come the same week that Germany’s government confirmed that Bundestag members had received Apple alerts about apparent spyware attacks.

Wiroj said preparations for the Dec 7–11 no-confidence debate remain secure but urged an investigation into possible interference in parliamentary scrutiny. He suggested referring the matter to the current chair of the House’s Committee on the Armed Forces, arguing that Apple’s security warnings warranted investigation.

title: Global renewable stocks surge after democrats sweep congress
article:
(Nov 4): Renewable energy stocks rallied around the world after the Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the US midterm elections, an outcome seen as supporting more favourable policy for the industry.

Denmark’s Orsted A/S, an operator of offshore wind farms, was the biggest gainer in Europe, rising as much as 8.1%, with Vestas Wind Systems A/S and SMA Solar Technology AG among others climbing.

In US premarket trading, First Solar Inc advanced as much as 9.2% and Sunrun Inc added as much as 9.4%.

That followed similar gains in Asia: South Korea’s Hanwha Solutions Corp surged 19%, while HD Hyundai Energy Solutions Co and OCI Holdings Co jumped 12% and 10% respectively.

According to Barclays plc analysts, the midterm results ease political risk on US renewables and supporting networks.

“It potentially reduces the risk of further political interference with renewable energy incentives and provides greater protection for the long-term economics of US wind, solar and battery storage investments,” the analysts led by Peter Crampton wrote in a research note.

See also: Saudi budget deficit more than doubles on war, Aramco fees

“This should help ease investor concerns around regulatory uncertainty, support confidence in future project returns and potentially drive a reduction in the risk premium applied to US renewable assets."

Investors see a Democratic wave as supportive of companies in the clean energy supply chain, including solar and batteries, at the expense of the traditional energy sector. Renewable stocks are also benefiting from a rotation away from artificial intelligence-related stocks.

“The blue trade is showing up already with money rotating out of the AI buildout and into what a Democratic Congress favours," said Anna Wu, an investment strategist and founder of Floodlines Research. Hanwha Solutions “benefits directly if a Democratic Congress pushes back on Trump’s anti-solar policy” as its Qcells business operates big US factories, she added.

See also: Eurozone 3Q growth beats estimates despite slump in France

JPMorgan Chase & Co strategists had said ahead of the midterms that a “blue wave” would be encouraging for clean-energy stocks through greater support on appropriations, oversight and permitting.

title: Eurozone wage growth to slow sharply next year in boost for ECB
article:
(Nov 4): Euro-area pay growth is poised to slow sharply in the third quarter of 2027, encouraging news for the European Central Bank as it battles inflation driven by the Iran war.

The ECB’s wage tracker, published Wednesday (Nov 4), predicts salaries will rise by an annual 2.4% between July and September next year. That’s below the forecast of 2.8% for the first and second quarters. All readings are far below 2024’s 5.3% peak.

Policymakers are particularly attentive to pay developments at present as they aim to stop energy-driven inflation from becoming entrenched through wages and firms boosting prices. Inflation expectations among euro-area households increased slightly again in September.

The ECB kept interest rates unchanged last week following quarter-point hikes in June and September. But officials are ready to raise again next month if the inflation outlook doesn’t improve.

Wages don’t show a material response at this stage, the ECB said last week. But it listed the possibility of stronger-than-expected pay increases as one factor contributing to upside risks to the outlook. Some officials argue the ECB cannot just wait for such outcomes to materialise, as acting only at that stage could be too late.

title: China boosts market defence with National Team, buybacks
article:
(Nov 4): China escalated its defence of the stock market, as state-backed funds answered the government’s rallying call by increasing purchases and more companies stepped up buyback plans.

A basket of nine exchange-traded funds that are favoured by the so-called national team of investors drew RMB76.7 billion of inflows on Tuesday, according to Bloomberg-compiled data. That was the second largest on record. Turnover for those funds came in at around RMB83 billion on Wednesday, higher than in most sessions this quarter.

The funds have been accelerating purchases since last month but the spike in buying followed the government’s rollout of liquidity-injection measures this week aimed at reinvigorating the market. The tech-heavy Star 50 Index surged nearly 10% on Wednesday, its best session since July, also boosted by news that Chinese AI developers may receive just a fraction of the advanced Nvidia Corp chips, potentially fuelling demand for domestic alternatives.

“The latest developments in the market point to Beijing’s growing recognition that more support is needed,” said Homin Lee, senior macro strategist at Lombard Odier in Singapore. “At the same time, the authorities seem to focus more on technical tweaks,” suggesting a perception that the status quo is roughly manageable, he added.

The CSI 300 Index gained more than 2%. The rebound also tracked a broad move higher in Asia as investors digested the US midterm election results and considered the latest selloff as excessive.

See also: China plans broad AI guardrails after global security lapses

Chinese companies are also being enlisted in the effort to shore up confidence. CXMT Corp's chairman proposed Wednesday to increase the size of its share buyback to between RMB2.5 billion and RMB5 billion, saying the move was intended to protect investors’ interests and bolster confidence.

In a rare move in the market, Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co’s controlling shareholders have proposed returning at least RMB1 billion to investors in 2026 through cash dividends and share buybacks.

The buyback plans came after the People’s Bank of China said it would cut the rate on its relending facility to 1% from 1.25%, make the programme permanent and encourage banks to increase lending. The facility provides low-cost central bank funding to banks for loans that finance companies’ share buybacks and stake increases by major shareholders.

See also: Chinese stock sell-off resumes as rescue tools face scepticism

Chinese banks have already submitted applications for more than RMB200 billion of relending quotas, the PBOC said.

Meanwhile, several other mainland-listed companies — including Ningbo Joyson Electronic Corp, Universal Scientific Industrial Shanghai Co and Hwatsing Technology Co — disclosed new share buyback plans. Ningbo Joyson proposed buying back between RMB150 million and RMB300 million, according to its filing.

title: Saudi budget deficit more than doubles on war, Aramco fees
article:
(Nov 4): Saudi Arabia’s quarterly fiscal deficit more than doubled as the kingdom’s oil revenues tumbled on the back of disruptions from the US-Iran war and lower fees paid by state oil giant Aramco.

The government posted a budget shortfall of SAR84 billion in the third quarter, up about 145% from the prior period, according to a statement from the Finance Ministry on Tuesday.

Oil receipts fell almost 40% from the prior quarter to about SAR116 billion, the lowest level since 2020. Non-oil revenues fell around 7%, while overall spending dipped by 8%.

Economists including Monica Malik at Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank and Tim Callen of the Arab Gulf States Institute said changes in government payments from Aramco help explain some of the drop in oil revenue.

Aramco, in which the government is the top shareholder, pays less in royalty fees when average realised oil prices are lower, as they were in the third quarter, Callen said. Income tax factors also resulted in lower fees.

See also: Eurozone 3Q growth beats estimates despite slump in France

The higher deficit underscores the fiscal strain Saudi Arabia is under as conflict in the Middle East disrupts exports of crude oil — the kingdom’s biggest single source of earnings — and drives elevated wartime spending. It also dovetails with an economic contraction of 3.8% over the same time period, mostly due to depressed oil activities.

The US-Iran war, which broke out on Feb 28 and is at risk of flaring up in coming weeks, has threatened Saudi infrastructure, disrupted oil output and effectively closed the Strait of Hormuz, the Persian Gulf chokepoint through which most pre-war oil exports flowed.

The world’s largest oil exporter has managed to offset some of the impact of the war by using a backup pipeline to move crude to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. It’s now exporting crude at some of the highest levels of the war and is benefiting from higher oil prices.

See also: AI darling Taiwan extends economic growth run unseen since 1987

Brent crude in London last closed around US$104 a barrel.

Callen, a former International Monetary Fund mission chief for Saudi Arabia, expects oil revenues to “rebound strongly” in the fourth quarter, in part because of stronger crude prices and higher Aramco royalties.

He sees Saudi Arabia’s 2026 fiscal deficit at around 6% of gross domestic product, higher than the government forecast for 4.9%. ADCB’s Malik predicts a shortfall of 5.6% of GDP.

“The oil revenue surprised to the downside in the third quarter, given the oil market fundamentals, though [it] is in line with the Aramco payments to the government,” Malik said. “This places risks to a wider deficit than we are currently forecasting.”

Should Saudi oil exports continue and Brent stay near the US$105 level, the kingdom stands to make an additional US$8 billion in oil revenue across October and November, according to Mohamed Abu Basha, head of macroeconomic analysis at investment bank EFG Hermes.

At the same time, the kingdom has increased its forecast for spending amid expectations it will need to direct more money to defence and infrastructure to support the economy.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Expenditure needs may only have increased since the end of the third quarter as Saudi Arabia has faced escalating threats from the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.

In October, they stepped up attacks on the capital, Riyadh, killing more than a dozen people, curbing air travel and delaying major showpiece events.

The International Monetary Fund has said Saudi Arabia’s fiscal buffers and backup oil-export facilities are helping curb damage to the economy. It still sees the kingdom as better placed than its Gulf peers to ride out the upheaval.

Saudi Arabia said it plans to continue borrowing in public and private markets to plug its fiscal deficit and said it remains flexible in its ability to adjust spending to face economic and geopolitical changes.

title: Franc, yen emerge as FX winners as US midterms weaken dollar
article:
(Nov 4): The Swiss franc and Japanese yen jumped as US election results pointed to the Democrats winning both the House and the Senate, sending the dollar to its worst day in a month.

The franc rose almost 1% and the yen 0.7% in Asian trading, the biggest gains among major currencies as investors sought haven-like assets. Bloomberg’s dollar index fell as much as 0.4%, the most since Oct 2 while the risk-sensitive Australian dollar lagged peers.

Democrats are projected to flip control of the House and Senate in an election dominated by rising cost of living concerns. A sweep of Congress may herald tighter regulatory scrutiny, particularly of artificial intelligence companies, and restrain further government spending to constrain price pressure.

The prospect of tougher oversight weighed on equities, with AI-linked stocks seen as particularly vulnerable. S&P 500 Index futures fell as much as 1.4% while Nasdaq 100 contracts slid as much as 2.4%.

“The US dollar’s Achilles’ heel is being exposed” with its fortunes tied to the AI boom, said David Forrester, a senior strategist at Credit Agricole CIB in Singapore. “A Democrat blue wave that stifles datacentre buildouts and hobbles the AI boom would weigh on the US dollar.

See also: Onshore yuan snaps winning streak as PBOC lifts FX reserve ratio

Still, the pressure on the dollar may not last. Oil prices could rebound if US-Iran talks aimed at avoiding a return to all-out war fail, potentially lifting inflation expectations, raising bets on further Federal Reserve rate hikes and giving the dollar a boost. Trump also retains the ability to veto congressional efforts to constrain his policy agenda.

“Even if the Democrats win both houses of Congress, US President Trump is likely to veto any efforts to tighten AI regulations and introducing such regulations would be difficult from the perspective of competition with China,” said Rinto Maruyama, a senior strategist at SMBC Nikko Securities. “Eventually, there will likely be a reversal of the dollar’s weakness.”

title: Dubai firm raises US$529 mil in UAE’s first IPO of the year
article:
(Nov 4): Dubai Investments PJSC raised US$529 million from the sale of shares in DIP Holding plc, pushing ahead with the United Arab Emirates’ first listing of the year despite a regional war that has weighed on markets.

DIP Holding’s sole shareholder sold a 20% stake, or about 1.7 billion shares, at AED1.12 apiece, valuing the company at about AED9.7 billion, according to a statement Wednesday (Nov 4). The price was at the midpoint of the marketed range, an unusual outcome for UAE IPOs, which overwhelmingly price at the top.

The offering was significantly oversubscribed, the company said in the statement, without specifying the level of demand.

DIP’s order book included a large number of local family offices, among them major groups that are also shareholders in parent Dubai Investments, as well as prominent conglomerate Al Tayer Group, Bloomberg News has reported. The offering also drew some international funds, though demand was more heavily skewed toward local investors than in other recent UAE listings.

DIP is offering investors US$592 million in dividend payouts over the next three years, implying a dividend yield of about 7.5%, toward the high end of the range initially marketed. Some investors had pushed for higher payouts given geopolitical concerns, Bloomberg News reported.

Shares are expected to begin trading on Dubai’s bourse on Nov 11.

See also: Temasek’s Mapletree said to pick banks for Singapore IPO

DIP owns Dubai Investments Park, a 2,300ha mixed-use development established in 1997 that includes warehouses, hotels, shops, schools and medical centres.

The offering comes amid a sharp slowdown in Gulf IPO activity, with the regional war adding to existing pressure on share sales. Stocks have declined across much of the region since the conflict began in late February, with Dubai’s benchmark down about 11%.

title: Indonesia arrests ex-police chief for alleged wiretap of Prabowo
article:
(Nov 4): Indonesia’s former national police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo and two other top police officials were arrested Tuesday for allegedly illegally wiretapping Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto and numerous others in government and civil society, prompting a pledge for a broad review of surveillance powers.

Listyo, who was recently appointed as the presidential chief of staff, and the other two suspects also allegedly tapped the phone numbers of politicians, media figures and civil society leaders between 2025 and 2026, according to a briefing in Jakarta late on Tuesday. Police criminal investigation chief Asep Safrudin identified the suspects by their initials LSP, ASN and EH.

The full scale of the alleged surveillance operation and its purpose remain unclear. Investigators seized 11 mobile phones, an iPad and four flash drives, questioning 10 witnesses and three experts. Police have not disclosed how many people were monitored, what information was obtained or who may have received the intercepted communications.

Investigators allege that phone numbers were entered into the police’s lawful interception management system without the required verification or any legitimate law enforcement purpose. The suspects also allegedly ordered the deletion of electronic records in October to conceal the activities, according to police.

The government plans to review surveillance powers across security and law enforcement agencies, in coordination with the national cyber and encryption agency, senior law minister Yusril Ihza Mahendra said in a separate briefing late Tuesday.

Yusil described the three suspects as senior police officials, with LSP having the rank of general. Local media, including Kompas and the Jakarta Globe, identified LSP as being Listyo Sigit Prabowo. He is not related to the president.

See also: Swiss inflation accelerates to highest in almost three years

All three are being held at the national police headquarters in Jakarta. They face potential prison terms of up to 10 years under one of the provisions cited by police.

Listyo, who could not immediately be reached for comment, saw his career flourish under the previous president, Joko Widodo, who employed him as a presidential police aide-de-camp before appointing him national police chief in 2021. The arrest comes roughly a month after Listyo was removed as police chief and made presidential chief of staff.

Prabowo also awarded him one of Indonesia’s highest civilian honours on Oct 1. Less than three weeks before his arrest, Listyo met privately with the president at the palace, where he was instructed to oversee key government programmes, according to the cabinet secretary. Authorities have yet to discuss a replacement for Listyo as a presidential chief of staff, Yusril said.

Listyo’s recent reassigment was part of a broader reshuffle involving figures closely associated with Widodo, also known as Jokowi. Pratikno, who served as Jokowi’s state secretary, was made head of the presidential advisory council. Another ally, Muhammad Qodari, became its secretary.

“I think this will heighten tensions between Jokowi and Prabowo,” said Nicky Fahrizal, a researcher specialising in law and security at the Jakarta-based Centre for Strategic and International Studies. That could potentially trigger wider political instability with consequences for the economy, he added.

The allegations represent a serious breach of the police’s longstanding ethos of loyalty to the president, Fahrizal said. He warned that a political settlement without full legal accountability would undermine public trust.

“If it is just allowed to fade away, it would set a bad precedent,” he said.

The investigation has also touched officials with personal ties to the president. Ahrie Sonta Nasution, identified by local media as another suspect, previously served as Listyo’s private secretary before becoming Prabowo’s police aide-de-camp in 2024. Listyo himself announced his selection.

Yusril said Prabowo had been informed of the investigation by the current police chief, Suyudi Ario Seto. Authorities are still investigating the motive and have found no indication so far that the alleged activities were linked to an attempt to overthrow the government.

The case adds to longstanding concerns over surveillance in Southeast Asia’s largest economy. A 2024 Amnesty International investigation documented the sale of invasive spyware to Indonesian companies and state agencies, including the national police. No connection has been established between those findings and the current investigation.

title: Temasek’s Mapletree said to pick banks for Singapore IPO
article:
(Nov 4): Mapletree Investments Pte Ltd, a real estate firm owned by Singapore state investor Temasek Holdings Pte Ltd, has picked banks for an initial public offering of parts of the company in the city state that could raise at least S$1 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.

Citigroup Inc, DBS Group Holdings Ltd and Morgan Stanley are working on the planned listing of some of Mapletree’s assets, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is confidential. The company has not yet decided which assets would be included, the people said, adding that a listing could take place as soon as next year.

Deliberations are ongoing and details such as the timing and size of the offer may change, they said. More banks may also be added later, the people added.

A representative for Temasek referred a request for comment to Mapletree, which declined to comment. Any material information, should it arise, will be communicated through the appropriate channels, the spokesperson for Mapletree added. Citi, DBS and Morgan Stanley declined to comment.

Mapletree recorded a rare loss in its 2023-2024 fiscal year, dragged by challenges including markdowns on its office assets in the US, Australia and Europe. It also has exposure to China, which continues to suffer from a major property downturn.

Mapletree oversees private funds and three listed real estate investment trusts in Singapore. Talks about a merger with CapitaLand Investment Ltd — another Temasek-backed property manager — stalled earlier this year due to disagreements on issues including valuation, leadership, personnel revamps and business performance, people familiar with the situation have said.

See also: Mapletree Investments prepares for IPO early next year

An IPO of Mapletree’s size would be a welcome lift for Singapore, which recently lost out on a potential US$1.5 billion listing of a real estate investment trust after data centre operator AirTrunk postponed the deal, Bloomberg News has reported.

First-time share sales have raised US$1.24 billion in Singapore this year, down 17% from a year ago, data compiled by Bloomberg show.

title: Clearbridge Health to acquire pipes and valves business for $2.76 mil
article:
Clearbridge Health, which listed back in 2017 as a provider of medical diagnostic services, plans to diversify into making and selling pipes and valves.

Clearbidge plans to acquire a group of businesses owned by Richard Koh Chye Heng, via an entity called Pan Asian Global, for $2.76 million.

The acquisition will be paid with $1.5 million in cash, plus $1.26 million in 630 million new Clearbridge shares to be issued at 0.2 cents each.

Upon completion of the deal, Koh will hold 8.91% of the enlarged share capital.

Clearbridge says the new business will let it tap Asia's rapid industrialisation, which has lifted demand for valves and pipes specifically mande for the water management and oil and gas industries.

To reflect the new business nature, which requires approval at an EGM to be called, Clearbridge will be renamed Duvalco Holdings.

See also: iX Biopharma says Orion Speciality Labs’ lack of state licence is ‘expected’ at current stage

Navi Corporate Advisory, an independent valuer, estimates the target companies to have a market value of between $4.79 million to $4.96 million, as at June 30, and also an NTA of around $2.83 million.

For the half year ended June 30, earnings attributable to the sale shares was $0.18 million.

title: Asian tech stocks to rise on AI rally amid US votes
article:
(Nov 4) : Asian tech stocks looked set to rise after a revival in the artificial-intelligence trade lifted Wall Street, as investors awaited the results of the US midterm elections.

Equity-index futures for South Korea and Taiwan pointed higher, while those for Australia fell. Contracts for Japanese stocks edged lower as traders returned from a holiday.

US chipmakers rallied, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index climbing 2.6% after a recent rout fueled by concerns over the scale of AI spending. The rebound lifted the Nasdaq 100 by 0.7%. Adding to the optimism, Super Micro Computer Inc. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. both gave stronger-than-expected revenue forecasts, while Meta Platforms Inc. drew solid demand for its first bond sale in six months.

Elsewhere, Brent crude hovered near US$104 a barrel on Tuesday as traders weighed conflicting signals on US-Iran peace talks. Treasury yields rose after US job openings climbed to a four-month high, while the dollar strengthened.

The rebound in technology shares now faces the US midterm results, which may remove a key source of uncertainty and refocus investors on the outlook for AI spending and geopolitical risks heading into year-end.

“The results could act as a clearing event removing some uncertainty, though developments around the AI theme and geopolitics are the primary forces driving markets heading into the final two months of the year,” said Angelo Kourkafas at Edward Jones.

See also: AMD forecast exceeds estimates after AI chip demand soars

Millions of Americans are casting ballots Tuesday in races that will determine control of Congress as well as a range of local issues. The first polls close at 6 p.m. Eastern time.

Polymarket is pricing roughly a 95% probability of Democrats taking the House of Representatives and about a 77% chance of winning the Senate, pointing to the possibility of a sweep of both chambers.

“Tuesday’s elections could reshape the balance of power in Washington,” said Ken Mahoney at Mahoney Asset Management. “This will be good to put behind us as it has been an anticipated volatility event for quite some time.”

See also: Chip stocks rally as bonds fall on US election day

Geopolitical risks remained in focus as oil swung in choppy trading while investors parsed conflicting signals on the trajectory of peace talks between the US and Iran.

Tehran and Washington are reviewing fresh proposals from mediators aimed at resolving their differences and avoiding a return to all-out war, according to a diplomat briefed on the matter, following limited US airstrikes overnight.

Meanwhile, signs of resilience in the US labor market pushed Treasury yields higher. Job openings unexpectedly rose in September to a four-month high, while layoffs fell to their lowest level since March 2025 and quits increased.

The data may give Federal Reserve policymakers more room to focus on persistent inflation after leaving interest rates unchanged last week. The central bank raised rates in September for the first time in three years.

“For now, all signs point to a solid labor market, even if it is difficult for pockets of workers – namely those who are unemployed,” Matthew Martin, senior US economist at Oxford Economics, wrote in a note.

title: AMD forecast exceeds estimates after AI chip demand soars
article:
(Nov 4) : Advanced Micro Devices Inc., a key challenger to Nvidia Corp. in artificial intelligence chips, gave a revenue forecast that exceeded analysts’ estimates, showing that demand for data center processors remains strong.

Fourth-quarter revenue will be US$17 billion, plus or minus 3%, the chipmaker said in a statement Tuesday. That easily topped the average analyst estimate of US$16.3 billion, helping send the shares up about 8% in late trading.

The outlook provided fresh evidence that AI spending is sustainable, soothing jittery investors. Shares of chipmakers and other tech companies have been battered in recent weeks over concerns about a bubble in the AI infrastructure industry.

“AMD’s earnings are simultaneously a test of its own performance and of the broader AI trade,” Emarketer analyst Jacob Bourne said in a note. The results “will give investors encouragement given the recent tech and semiconductor selloff, as investors increasingly scrutinize AI spending and its returns.”

AMD’s outlook — along with a strong forecast from server maker Super Micro Computer Inc. — helped spark a late-trading rally among AI equipment makers and cloud providers. Shares of companies from CoreWeave Inc. and Nebius Group NV to Dell Technologies Inc. and Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. all gained.

Under Chief Executive Officer Lisa Su, AMD has become one of the most important suppliers of processors and computers that operate at the heart of AI facilities, underpinning a flood of new services.

See also: Chip stocks rally as bonds fall on US election day

“Our fourth-quarter outlook reflects accelerating revenue and earnings growth, driven by strong demand across our data center portfolio,” Chief Financial Officer Jean Hu said in the statement.

Even with recent market turbulence, AMD shares have more than doubled this year. The company’s valuation reached US$1 trillion in September, putting it in an elite group.

The data center growth has helped AMD offset a slump in the personal computer market, where rising memory-chip costs have slowed production and depressed user demand. Intel Corp., AMD’s top rival in that field, suffered its worst stock decline in decades after a downbeat earnings report last week.

See also: S&P 500 falls as chip rout offsets US-Iran hopes

One possible weak spot for AMD: Its gross margin will narrow to about 55% in the fourth quarter. That measure — the percentage of sales after removing production costs — had been 56% in the previous period.

AMD’s third-quarter sales rose 45% to US$13.4 billion. Profit climbed to US$2.09 a share, minus certain items. Analysts on average had predicted revenue of US$13.1 billion and earnings of US$1.97 a share.

AMD continues to deliver record results and now boasts sales that are twice as big as they were two years ago. It’s also been outperforming longtime nemesis Intel in the market for central processing units, or CPUs. But the company is still well behind Nvidia in so-called AI accelerators, which are used to train and run artificial intelligence models.

Sales at AMD’s data center business nearly doubled to US$8.5 billion. Analysts had predicted a total of US$8.2 billion. PC and gaming-related sales shrank 8% to US$3.7 billion.

Like other makers of components for PCs, AMD is suffering from a side effect of the data center boom. AI servers require a massive amount of memory. That’s cut into the supply of chips available for laptops and desktop machines — and forced prices up.

AMD is debuting new product ranges in both the CPU and accelerator markets. The Santa Clara, California-based company is also taking on Nvidia more directly with its Helios server design.

But Nvidia, the largest chipmaker and world’s most valuable company, hasn’t been standing still. It’s updating its own lineup at a fast pace and branching out into everything from software to networking to complete computers.

title: Chip stocks rally as bonds fall on US election day
article:
(Nov 4) : A revival of the artificial-intelligence trade powered Wall Street gains, bonds fell and the dollar rose on US Election Day.

Chipmakers halted a selloff that had been fueled by worries the AI spending spree is becoming harder to justify. The rebound lifted the S&P 500 even as most of its firms fell. In late hours, Advanced Micro Devices Inc. and Super Micro Computer Inc. gave strong forecasts. Oil prices eased. But that wasn’t enough to lift Treasuries amid solid job openings data.

Millions of Americans across the country are casting ballots in races Tuesday that will determine local issues as well as control of Congress. The first polls close at 6 p.m. Eastern time.

“Tuesday’s elections could reshape the balance of power in Washington,” said Ken Mahoney at Mahoney Asset Management. “This will be good to put behind us as it has been an anticipated volatility event for quite some time.”

Since 1950, the S&P 500 has never been lower 12 months after a midterm election, noted Tom Essaye at The Sevens Report.

“The results could act as a clearing event removing some uncertainty, though developments around the AI theme and geopolitics are the primary forces driving markets heading into the final two months of the year,” said Angelo Kourkafas at Edward Jones.

See also: S&P 500 falls as chip rout offsets US-Iran hopes

November has historically been a favorable month for equities, but the recent tech weakness has raised questions about market leadership, Mahoney noted.

At Edward Jones, Brian Therien said the recent market rotation represented less of a rejection of AI’s potential than a reassessment of the price that investors are willing to pay for it.

“Markets still assign premium valuations to companies that demonstrate strong demand, rising AI-related revenue, and the ability to fund additional investment internally,” he said. “We continue to recommend an overweight allocation to equities, with a preference for US large- and mid-cap stocks, due in part to the relative strength of the US economy.”

See also: Trump says US-Canada trade deal is close after talks with Carney

Apollo Global Management Inc. said it plans to take a more defensive approach to its investments tied to AI, as the asset manager plows billions into financing the infrastructure buildout underpinning the technology.

“We know that society will use dramatically more computing power in the future,” that demand for chips will remain strong, “and that AI capabilities are improving at an extraordinary rate,” Apollo President Jim Zelter said on a call with analysts Tuesday. “What we don’t know is how pricing and economics will evolve.”
